standard.title: Create texts for diverse contexts and audiences
standard.description: create and present informative and imaginative texts for diverse contexts and purposes, selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and a range of features and conventions to engage different audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create texts for specific purposes, selecting vocabulary and structures deliberately (AC9LS8C05). They create for defined purposes. They have not yet created for genuinely diverse contexts and audiences simultaneously, used narrative perspective deliberately, or created texts for external community audiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and present informative and imaginative texts for diverse contexts and purposes — selecting vocabulary, structures and conventions to engage different audiences.

nodes.label: Selecting features for diverse audiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select vocabulary, expressions and conventions deliberately to engage specific and varied audiences — not only to meet a defined purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a text for a specified audience and identify at least three deliberate feature selections made to engage that audience.
nodes.typical_width: Create texts across informative and imaginative purposes with audience engagement as the primary design criterion; use varied vocabulary, structures and conventions suited to each audience; create digital and print texts that present views on issues for specific audiences.
wider: Create the same content for two contrasting audiences — explicitly contrast every vocabulary, structure and convention choice made for each
Create a text for an audience with no target language background — make deliberate decisions about what requires explanation and what can be assumed
nodes.hinge_reason: Designing language choices for audience engagement — not only for purpose — is the maturation of the text creation capability across the sequence. Students who only consider purpose without audience produce texts that are technically correct but communicatively flat.

response_modes.reason: Audience-oriented design requires metacognitive attention to the reader's perspective. Annotation tasks and contrastive production scaffold the audience-awareness that makes language choices genuinely communicative.

success_criteria: Creates a text for a specified audience with at least three deliberate feature selections identified
The text is consistently designed for audience engagement — not only purpose compliance

nodes.label: Creating across imaginative modes and narrative perspectives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create imaginative texts across varied modes — using different narrative perspectives, characters, settings and plot structures — to engage specific audiences.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one imaginative text using a deliberate narrative perspective — identifying why that perspective was chosen for the audience.
nodes.typical_width: Create stories, plays, scripts and dialogues across varied imaginative formats; use first, second and third person narration deliberately; create texts from multiple character perspectives; use description, dialogue and action to engage audiences; create cultural and community performance texts.
wider: Tell the same story from three different points of view — explaining what each perspective reveals and conceals for the audience
Create an imaginative text for a genuinely different cultural audience — reflecting on what needed to change to make it accessible and engaging for that audience

response_modes.reason: Narrative perspective and imaginative mode competence develops through creating across varied perspective conditions and text formats.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Using multiple narrative perspectives and imaginative modes with deliberate audience intent is where target language creative production reaches genuine literary sophistication.
success_criteria: Creates at least one imaginative text using a deliberate narrative perspective
Explains why the chosen perspective serves the intended audience

nodes.label: Creating for real and community audiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create and present texts for real community audiences — including target language community peers, First Nations Australian cultural contexts, and public occasions.
nodes.minimum_width: Create and present at least one text for a genuine audience outside the classroom — reflecting on whether it achieved its communicative purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Create texts for real community purposes — social media, school publications, community events, cultural exchanges with target language community peers; reflect on the impact of a visit to a significant cultural location and present in the target language; compose and perform speeches for real occasions; create cultural ID profiles for exchange with target language community peers.
wider: Create a text for a target language community peer exchange — receive and incorporate feedback about whether the text achieved its communicative purpose for that audience
Contribute to a First Nations cultural location text with appropriate permission — reflecting on the protocols followed and what they taught about cultural respect

response_modes.reason: Creating for real community audiences integrates all prior text creation capabilities — audience design (N1) and imaginative mode (N2) — and tests them in a genuine communicative context.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Creating for real community audiences — peer exchanges, public occasions, cultural contexts — is where the target language becomes a fully functional tool for genuine social participation.
success_criteria: Creates and presents at least one text for a genuine audience outside the classroom
Reflects on whether the text achieved its communicative purpose for that audience
